A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thompson-CHM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, references and complete supplied appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 Section 7 reports original Bernoulli-bandit simulations, including sample-complexity and sampling-allocation results in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v3 Section 6 retains these original simulation results in Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: The conditional posterior sampling, Bernoulli/categorical arm selection, stopping rules and interval adaptation are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Replacing CHF with CHM and Tresh with Thresh changes terminology, not procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate seven Bernoulli arms with means 0.1 through 0.7 under the same feasible and infeasible threshold scenarios. No additional datasets, tasks or empirical higher-dimensional evaluations appear.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain comparisons with theoretical sample-complexity bounds and optimal allocations. Neither version empirically evaluates additional competing algorithms; the discussed Murphy-sampling and thresholding methods remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported arm configuration, Beta prior, threshold grid, measurements and stopping-threshold formula are unchanged. v3's implementation attribution adds documentation without establishing a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The threshold sweep and empirical-versus-optimal allocation analysis in Figures 1–2 are retained. No ablations, robustness tests or additional empirical analyses are added or removed in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both Figure 2 captions specify estimates using 100 repetitions. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All four plot panels have identical graphical content across versions. Their sample-complexity curves, allocation results and accompanying empirical findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 5.1.2 corrects the reversed feasibility cases in v2 Section 6.1.2: matching thresholding-bandit complexity applies to the all-below-threshold infeasible case, while the claimed strict advantage applies to the feasible case. The numbered theorems, assumptions and appendix proofs otherwise retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of asymptotically optimal one-dimensional CHM identification, matching lower bounds, interval generalization and a potential higher-dimensional extension.

C2.justification: The corrected feasibility labels clarify when CHM is claimed to be easier than thresholding-bandit identification. The interpretations of sampling allocations and the unresolved higher-dimensional optimality limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 Section 6 newly states that the empirical implementation of T(x) comes from the cited Murphy-sampling work. v2 attributed the threshold function but did not explicitly identify this implementation provenance.

R1.justification: v3 removes v2's entire Related Work section, substantially reducing discussion of thresholding bandits, probabilistic hyperplane separability and fair sampling/Pareto fairness. Ten associated references disappear. The closest CHM, Murphy-sampling and top-two-sampling connections remain elsewhere.

P1.justification: v3 deletes the standalone related-work section, substantially shortens the main-text infeasible-case proof sketch, moves the two-stage strategy discussion into the sampling section, and places references before Appendix A. It also edits the introduction and standardizes CHM terminology.

P2.justification: The same figures and algorithm boxes are repositioned through document reflow; Figures 1–2 move from v2 page 12 to v3 page 11. Their axes, legends and captions remain unchanged, with no new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects a misleading feasibility-case comparison and clarifies implementation provenance, providing limited gains in accuracy and reproducibility. Removing related-work discussion and shortening the proof sketch reduce context, but the closest prior-work connections, appendix proofs and experimental evidence remain available.
